source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:12 (Bereshit Rabbah 84:13; the ten dotted places)
claim_en: The DOTTED ET: 'his brothers went to pasture ET their father's flock' — the object-word is dotted, says MS with the midrash: they went to pasture THEMSELVES, not the flock. SNAPSHOT carries BOTH dots on the two-letter word in-stream — the FIFTH of the ten dotted places reached, and the dotted layer holds instrumented.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:4 quoting the Ramah (Midrash Lekach Tov; Baal HaTurim; Kiddushin 66b named)
claim_en: The Ramah's peace-rule: 'every shalom-language in the Torah is FULL with vav except ONE lean — they could not speak to him le-shalom (to peace)' — the hatred too deep for the full word; Lekach Tov reads the lean skeleton as le-shalem, TO REPAY. The skeleton stands twice in the stream: here, and as the NAME Shillem in Naphtali's roster (Num 26:49) — a skeleton collision. (The rule's other wonder — the SEVERED vav of 'My covenant of peace', Num 25:12, read in Kiddushin — is a letter-form fact the instrument cannot see; named.)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:6 (the Great Masorah's seventeen; the Hilleli and Yerushalmi codices)
claim_en: aleihem ('to them') written FULL with yod: the Hilleli codex full, the Yerushalmi codex lean — and MS rules full, 'one of the SEVENTEEN full in the Torah by the Masorah.' SNAPSHOT verifies the count WHOLE: exactly seventeen full tokens in the Torah — and THREE of them stand in this chapter (37:6 the dream-telling, 37:13 the sending, 37:18 the conspiracy).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:16 quoting the Ramah (Kitzur Baal HaTurim)
claim_en: efo ('WHERE are they pasturing?'): the Ramah — 'in the Torah one alone is written with yod and final he: tell me now WHERE'; all its fellows are efo with vav and final aleph. Joseph's where-word shares its skeleton only with the honest EPHAH-measure pair of Deut 25:14-15 (a second collision); the Kitzur reads the yod-spelling as a hint — HERE (po) the evil began that crowned Jeroboam at Shechem.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:16 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: The rule's other half exact: efo with vav and final aleph stands FOUR times — Isaac's two tremblings, Jacob's 'if so, then', and Moses' 'wherein now shall it be known'.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:20 (the Hilleli; the Ramah; against the Great Masorah's muddle)
claim_en: ha-borot ('one of the PITS'): MS untangles the Masorah notes and rules lean-first-vav, full-second — the Hilleli, the precise books, and the Ramah agree; SNAPSHOT writes exactly that, once in the Torah. The Ramah's counter-sign — the ONE doubly-lean pit-word, the hewn cisterns of Deut 6:11 — stands at its address (asserted at build).

source: Minchat Shai + Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 37:24 (Bereshit Rabbah 84:12)
claim_en: va-yiqachuhu ('and they took him') written LEAN — no vav — and the midrash reads the singular-looking skeleton: WHO took him? SIMEON — repaid measure for measure when Joseph 'took from them Simeon' (42:24). The skeleton stands twice in the Torah: here, and Balak taking Balaam to the field of watchers (Num 23:14). (MS also files the dissent: Midrash Mishle gives the pit to Simeon AND Levi; both stand named.)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:25 quoting the Ramah
claim_en: holkhim ('a caravan of Ishmaelites... GOING down to Egypt'): 'this alone is full with vav AND yod in the Torah of its language.' Exact — and the lean-vav form's one station is Exod 33:15: 'if Your face does not GO'. The Torah's only doubly-full walkers carry Joseph down; the lean walkers are the Presence going up.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:33 quoting the Ramah (against the Hilleli and the Meiri)
claim_en: va-yakirah ('and he RECOGNIZED it'): the Hilleli copy and the Meiri's scroll-book wrote it lean; the Ramah rules FULL with yod — 'the precise texts dispute the lean note, and it is an error' — citing the Masorah's own three-lean list (he-knew-them and he-made-himself-strange, both 42:7, with Elijah's station outside). SNAPSHOT writes the full yod: the stream against the Hilleli again.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 37:24 (the Masorah)
claim_en: req ('the pit was EMPTY') — the Kitzur's Masorah pair, both Torah-side and EXACT: the empty pit (water it had none — but snakes and scorpions it had), and 'for it is no EMPTY word for you' (Deut 32:47): the one other empty-word in the stream.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 37:7 (the Masorah)
claim_en: va-tishtachavena ('and your sheaves BOWED') — the Kitzur's pair, both Torah-side and EXACT: the sheaves' bow in the dream, and 'the handmaids drew near and BOWED' (33:6) — though the first dream showed only eleven brothers, the whole house came to bow.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 37:32 (Sotah 10b)
claim_en: haker-na ('RECOGNIZE, please') — the Kitzur's Masorah pair: with the very phrase Judah deceived his father he was repaid — 'recognize, please, whose are the seal and cords' (38:25, the NEXT unit's span). The bare recognize-imperative stands three times in the Torah, all in Jacob's house (Laban's search 31:32 without na); joined to na exactly at the coat and the pledge.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 37:7/22/23/25/27/28 (six pointing notes)
claim_en: MS's pointing set across the chapter: le-ekhol ('to eat bread' — sitting down over the pit) with the aleph in hataf segol (the compound half-vowel), CHECKED in-stream; va-yimshekhu ('and they DREW him up') with pashta (the post-positive stroke) at word-end, and the soft letters — tesubena's tav, the two vo-bets of Reuben's plea and Judah's our-flesh, kutanto's tav with qamatz alone — all asserted at build.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:10 (ledger gen_60 row 5, reading pass 2026-08-28)
claim_en: THE FIVE SHEAF-WORDS AND THE FIVE PROSTRATIONS: the sheaf-noun ‹אֲלֻמָּה› ("alumah" — 'sheaf') occurs in the whole Torah ONLY in this verse, three times bare plus a fourth carrying the prefixed lamed (‹לַאֲלֻמָּתִי› "la-alumati" — 'to my sheaf'), and the binding-verb ‹מְאַלְּמִים› ("me'almim" — 'binding sheaves') makes a fifth word of the same three letters. The reading counts those five and reads the dream's prostration as fivefold.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:16 + Onkelos Gen 37:33 (ledger gen_60 row 8 and O2) joined at derivation to Exodus 22:12
middah: E7 (equal decree / same wording in two passages; I2 at law strength)
claim_en: THE BROTHERS STAGE THE BAILEE'S DEFENCE. Jacob's verdict is the doubled tearing-formula ‹טָרֹף טֹרָף› ("tarof toraf" — 'torn, surely torn'). That doubled pair of the tearing-root stands in exactly three places in the Torah: here (the father's verdict), Gen 44:28 (Judah quoting the verdict back, gen_67's span), and EXODUS 22:12 — ‹אִם טָרֹף יִטָּרֵף יְבִאֵהוּ עֵד הַטְּרֵפָה לֹא יְשַׁלֵּם› ('if it is surely torn, let him bring it as evidence — he shall not pay'), the keeper's exemption. Joseph's brothers were keepers of the flock (37:2), and they produce the bloodied tunic as evidence of a tearing: the exact procedure by which the later law releases a keeper from liability. The received translation renders the doubled formula identically at both Genesis seats ('surely killed'), flattening the tearing the law depends on.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:7 (ledger gen_60 row 2, reading pass 2026-08-28)
claim_en: THE THREE SLANDERS AND THEIR THREE REPAYMENTS, on the scales of Proverbs 16:11: what Joseph reported of his brothers is repaid to him measure for measure — the limb-of-a-living-animal charge repaid by 'they slaughtered a goat' (37:31); calling the handmaids' sons slaves repaid by 'Joseph was sold as a slave' (Psalms 105:17); the charge about the girls repaid by 'his master's wife cast her eyes upon him' (39:7, gen_62's span). Recorded as a three-row repayment table anchored on this verse's report-clause and discharged across the next two blocks.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:11 + 97:4 + Bereshit Rabbah 6:9 (ledger gen_60 rows 6, 21 and the 6:9 credit)
claim_en: THE DREAM AS AN ENFORCEABLE INSTRUMENT: the second dream is read not as prediction but as title, and enforced generations later — Joshua addresses the sun at Gibeon as 'wayward slave, were you not PURCHASED with my father's money? did my father not see you bowing in the dream?' before commanding it to stand still. Witness-tier: the dream's standing as an instrument is testimony carried from the reading, not derivable from the verse's grammar.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:22 (ledger gen_60 row 13, reading pass 2026-08-28)
claim_en: THE DEED-CHAIN IS A RECORDED DISPUTE, never decided: R. Yudan counts FOUR bills of sale (brothers to Ishmaelites to merchants to Midianites to Egypt), R. Huna counts FIVE (adding the state treasury, from which Potiphar then buys). Carried as a dispute; the machine records the sale event without fixing the number of conveyances.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:18 (ledger gen_60 row 10, reading pass 2026-08-28)
claim_en: TWO STANDING LAWS PRICED FROM THE SALE: the twenty pieces of silver are read as five sela'im, and the firstborn-redemption measure of five sela'im is decreed measure for measure — 'you sold Rachel's firstborn for twenty'; the same twenty divided among the brothers gives the half-shekel beka a head (Exod 38:26). A law-shaped claim resting on this verse's own number.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 84:12 (ledger gen_60 row 22, reading pass 2026-08-28)
claim_en: THE DREAM IS LOGGED: 'his father kept the matter' — R. Levi says he took a quill and wrote down the day, the hour and the place; R. Chiyya reads the Divine Spirit saying KEEP, for these are destined to occur. The verse is read as the creation of a dated record, which is what makes the later fulfilment auditable rather than merely remembered.

source: Onkelos Genesis 37:3 (ledger gen_60 O1) with Bereshit Rabbah 84:8 (row 3)
claim_en: THE LOVE-REASON IS DECIDED IN TRANSLATION: 'a son of his OLD AGE' ‹בֶן זְקֻנִים› ("ben zequnim") is rendered by the received translation as 'a WISE son' ("bar chakkim"), voting with R. Nechemya — that Jacob transmitted to Joseph everything he had received from Shem and Ever — against the plain chronological sense and against R. Yehuda's face-likeness reading. Dual-track: the machine carries the age-sense from the grammar and the wisdom-sense as the translation's witnessed reading.
